To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a fully implicit finite-difference scheme for the unsteady Navier-Stokes equation based on the one step @q-method in time and the vectorial operator splitting for discretization in space can be used to compute solutions of high accuracy and that it has excellent stability properties.

the proposed algorithm is unconditionally stable and convergent, that it can be used for the solution of the incompressible Navies-Stokes equations on a structured Cartesian mesh with arbitrary topology, and that it is easy to implement.
we present a fully implicit, unconditionally stable, second-order accurate, and efficient method for the solution of the unsteady in-compressible Navier-Stoke equations on Cartesian grids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new time stepping method for solving the unsteady in- compressible Navier-Stoke equations.
the development of a new time stepping method for the solution of incompressible Navie-Stokes flows.
the development of efficient and robust methods for solving the Navier-Stokes equation.

the proposed method is a good candidate for large scale applications.
the method is very robust with respect to the Reynolds number and to the time step.
the proposed approach is very efficient and robust.

the method is very stable and robust.
we are able to simulate complex flows at high Reynolds numbers with a fully implicit scheme.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the vectorial operator splitting approach is a very efficient way to treat the nonlinearity in the incompressible Navies-Stokes equations and that the @q-method is a very good candidate for time stepping.
vectorial operator splitting can be combined with the fully discrete @q-method to yield a robust numerical method for the incompressible Naviers-Stokes equations.
the @q-method is a very promising approach for solving the unsteady incompresible Navier-Stoke equations.
